sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Prefix sum is a key **preprocessing** technique: spend linear time building a table once, then answer range queries in [[primary|constant time]].
items: Build a new array **P** where P[i] is the sum of A from index 0 to i
The sum of range [L, R] is [[primary|P[R] - P[L-1]]]
When L = 0, just use P[R]; an extra **sentinel cell** handles this uniformly

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Repeated summing is concentrated in preprocessing, so each query never has to walk the range again.
items: **Space complexity**: [[warning|O(n)]] for the extra prefix array
Versus re-summing each query at [[danger|O(n)]], it pays off more the more queries you run

sections.heading: Extensions
sections.content: The prefix-sum idea extends to many other settings.
items: **2D prefix sum**: use inclusion-exclusion to get any sub-rectangle sum in O(1)
**Difference array**: the inverse operation, ideal for many range-add updates
Combined with a **hash map**, it solves problems like "subarray sum equals K"
**Limit**: if the array changes, switch to a Fenwick tree or segment tree
